laws.rule: Penalties for drug offences are severe. This includes long prison sentences in local jails. Authorities may arrest you for illegal drugs if you're either: carrying even a very small amount of drugs, or with someone who's using them If you're found driving under the influence of alcohol or other drugs, authorities will arrest and possibly detain you. Border officials may screen you for drugs, including on departure. - Carrying and using drugs
laws.heading: Drugs

laws.rule: Avoid public displays of affection. Same-sex relationships are legal in Dominican Republic , but the country is conservative. Same-sex marriages aren't recognised in Dominican Republic. It's not illegal to discriminate based on sexual orientation or gender identity.
laws.heading: LGBTQIA+ travellers

laws.rule: For trips of less than 3 months, you can drive with: an International Driving Permit (IDP) an Australian driver's licence You must get your IDP before you leave Australia. - Driving or riding
laws.heading: Driving permit

laws.rule: Drones of 0.25 kg or more must be registered with IDAC and flown by a licensed remote pilot; under 249 g needs no licence or insurance. A visitor flying in restricted areas, commercially or outside RAD-107 applies on form IDAC 1500-9 at least five working days ahead (about fifteen working days is typical). A foreigner whose home country does not require licence or registration for that drone attaches that country's rule and an ID. Maximum 400 ft above ground, no flying over people, and no flying in airspace other than Class G without IDAC approval. Foreigners may fly commercially for now only if hired by a Dominican company.
laws.heading: Drone operations for visitors

laws.rule: No tax is charged for carrying money, but if you enter or leave with more than US$10,000 (or the equivalent in pesos or another currency, or bearer securities) you must declare it to customs officers on the official form and show documents proving the money's lawful source. US$10,000 is about A$14,200 (RBA 30 Oct 2026: A$1 = USD 0.7040).

Duty-free for adults: up to 5 litres of alcoholic drinks. Tobacco duty-free: 20 packs of cigarettes, or 25 cigars, or 200 grams of tobacco. Gifts are limited to US$500 in total, usable once every three months.

Medicines for personal use are allowed. For controlled or psychotropic substances you must show the medical prescription that justifies their use during your stay. Plants, farm products, food and medicines can also be regulated by the Ministry of Agriculture or the Ministry of Public Health.

drone-pilot-pathway.summary: IDAC (Dominican civil aviation institute) requires registration and a remote pilot licence for drones over 0.25 kg, and a permit (form 1500-9) for commercial or restricted-area flights. Foreigners may operate commercially for now only when hired by a Dominican company.

items.text: No public register of licensed drone operators was found on the IDAC drone pages.

A remote pilot licence is needed for drones over 0.25 kg: at least 18 years old, a theory test and a practical flight test; existing pilots can validate a licence and skip the theory test. Commercial or restricted-area flights need a special permit: form IDAC 1500-9 with the operator licence, drone registration, insurance where applicable and a map with coordinates. IDAC asks for at least five working days' notice and gives about fifteen working days as the usual time.

IDAC's FAQ answers 'Can I do commercial operations as a foreigner?' with: for now they are allowed only if a Dominican company hires them and requests it. A foreigner whose home country requires no licence or registration for that drone weight attaches the relevant part of that country's rules and an ID copy to the application.

Airspace other than Class G needs prior approval from IDAC's flight standards operations department in coordination with air traffic control; prohibited or restricted areas, including near government or military sites, need the same permission.
